name: Voskhod 2
dispatch: Voskhod 2 achieved the first spacewalk and nearly turned it into the first death in space. Alexei Leonov floated out of an inflatable airlock into vacuum, the first human ever fully outside a spacecraft — and then his suit ballooned so stiff he couldn't bend to get back in. He had to open a valve and bleed his own air out, courting the bends, just to shrink enough to fit through the hatch. It wasn't over: the automatic reentry failed, the crew flew down by hand, and they landed hundreds of kilometres off course in the frozen Siberian forest, where they waited out two nights among wolves before rescuers reached them on skis. The public saw twelve triumphant minutes; how close it came stayed secret for years.
description: Pavel Belyayev + Alexei Leonov's 1-day flight — first EVA in history. Leonov spent 12 min outside Voskhod 2 (1965-03-18 11:34 UTC), pressurised through an inflatable Volga airlock that Soviet engineers added because the Voskhod hull lacked the room for full depressurisation. Leonov's suit ballooned in vacuum, jamming him outside the airlock; he had to vent suit pressure to re-enter, raising decompression-sickness risk. Re-entry was equally dramatic — the automatic landing system failed, and Belyayev manually piloted the descent module to a hard landing in deep Urals snow ~390 km off-target; the crew survived two nights in the forest among wolves before rescue helicopters arrived 1965-03-21. The cabin atmosphere also became O₂-rich in orbit, after the EVA hatch failed to re-seal, briefly risking spontaneous combustion.

events.label: LAUNCH
events.note: Voskhod 11A57 from Baikonur Site 1 (Gagarin's Start) 1965-03-18 07:00 UTC.

events.label: ORBIT INSERT
events.note: Insertion into 167 × 475 km Earth orbit, 64.8° inclination.

events.label: EVA
events.note: Leonov exits the Volga airlock 1965-03-18 11:34 UTC; first human EVA. 12 min outside; suit ballooned in vacuum and he vented pressure to re-enter.

events.label: DEORBIT
events.note: Automatic landing system fails; Belyayev manually pilots descent. 390 km off-target hard landing in Perm Oblast snow.

events.label: RESCUE
events.note: Crew survived 2 nights in -30°C wolf-inhabited forest before recovery helicopters reached them 1965-03-21.
